facts.text: On this date in 1960, the US launched Echo 1 — a 100-foot metallic balloon visible to the naked eye that served as the world's first communications satellite by simply bouncing radio signals off its surface.
On August 12, 1981, IBM released the first PC. Within a decade, the company had lost control of the standard it created, ceding the market to clone-makers it had licensed the architecture to.
Manila is the most densely populated city on Earth, packing over 111,000 people per square kilometer — denser than any neighborhood in New York, Tokyo, or Mumbai.
More people live inside a circle drawn 4,000 km around Bangladesh's capital Dhaka than outside it — roughly half of all humanity fits within that single radius.
Canada has more lakes than every other country combined, holding about 60% of the world's fresh surface lake water, yet ranks among the most sparsely populated nations on Earth.
On August 12, 1981, IBM launched its first personal computer at a price of $1,565 — roughly $5,400 today. Within three years, IBM PC clones had already begun eating the market it created.
On August 12, 1992, NAFTA was finalized after 14 months of negotiations. U.S.-Mexico trade has since grown from $81 billion to over $800 billion annually.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792 by 24 brokers. The tree blew down in a storm in 1865 — the exchange outlasted it by about 160 years and counting.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit a $2 trillion market cap in 2022, making it the most valuable company in history. Its annual profit that year exceeded the entire GDP of New Zealand.
The S&P 500 has closed higher on the Friday before a three-day weekend roughly 65% of the time since 1950 — a pattern traders call the 'holiday effect' and academics still struggle to fully explain.
On this date in 1877, Asaph Hall discovered Deimos, Mars's outer moon — a captured asteroid so small that standing on its surface, you could throw a baseball into orbit.
Your skeleton is not static. Every 10 years, nearly all your bone mass has been silently dissolved and rebuilt, atom by atom, by cells that never rest.
On this date in 1960, the first passive communications satellite, Echo 1, was launched — a 100-foot aluminized balloon that bounced phone calls off its skin from orbit.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
The human eye can detect a single photon of light in total darkness. Your visual system is not limited by physics — it is limited only by neural noise filtering the signal out.
On this day in 1877, Asaph Hall began the observations that would lead him to discover Mars's two moons — four nights later, he almost quit, but his wife Angelina told him to keep looking.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. The pyramid is just that old.
On this day in 1981, IBM released the 5150 personal computer. It was already obsolete by design — IBM's own engineers knew it, and published the specs openly, expecting it to fail.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — before the telephone. Alexander Bain's 'electric printing telegraph' could transmit images across wires while most of the world still traveled by horse.
Oxford University began teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. When Montezuma was crowned, Oxford had already been educating scholars for three centuries.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 2012, it spread so fast linguists now debate whether invented words can go feral.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed. Untranslatable into English, it folds nostalgia, grief, and belonging into a single breath.

On this day in 1851, Isaac Singer received a patent for his sewing machine — and the word 'serendipity,' coined by Horace Walpole in 1754, was still so obscure most Americans had never encountered it.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Another Koenig coinage, but it borrowed Latin roots so convincingly that readers assume it is centuries old.

On August 12, 1981, IBM launched the personal computer — and the word 'cyberspace' did not yet exist. William Gibson invented it the following year, scribbling it on paper because he owned no computer.

On Aug 12, 2017, Bitcoin Cash completed its first difficulty adjustment after the BCH/BTC split — mining profitability arbitrage between the two chains caused wild hash rate swings that nearly stalled BCH blocks for days.

On Aug 12, 2020, Yam Finance collapsed within 35 hours of launch after a rebase bug minted uncontrolled governance tokens, destroying $750M in locked value and becoming DeFi's clearest early lesson in unaudited code risk.

The Bitcoin genesis block contains the embedded text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — Satoshi's timestamp proof doubles as a political statement, making the chain's origin block unreproducible without that specific headline.

Ethereum's EIP-1559, live since Aug 2021, has burned over 4 million ETH in base fees — turning the network's own transaction demand into a permanent supply sink without any central authority controlling the burn rate.

The largest single Bitcoin transaction by output value moved 500,000 BTC in a 2011 wallet consolidation by Satoshi-era miners — it remains unspent, sitting in addresses that have never interacted with any exchange.

On this date in 2006, Geoffrey Hinton published 'A Fast Learning Algorithm for Deep Belief Nets,' reviving interest in deep networks after a decade of neglect — the paper that quietly restarted modern AI.
On August 12, 2011, Google quietly acquired Motorola for $12.5B; buried in the deal was a team that would later seed Google Brain, reshaping how the company thought about machine intelligence.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,600 average US households, for a single model.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins before most structural biologists had reviewed even a fraction of them — it produced in months what the field had spent 50 years attempting.
The first neural network to defeat a human champion at Go, AlphaGo, used a policy network trained on 30 million board positions just to decide where to look — before the actual tree search began.
